Figure 8. Students Flowchart of StudentShield System

The student process offers a full range of tools that enable one to communicate their feelings and report any incidents. After going through the process of safe sign-in, there are two main options available. With the Safe Space model, one can post messages regarding their emotions. This tool enables one to decide whether they wish to contact a guardian or keep the record anonymous. The use of an organized gateway makes it possible for the person to identify themselves as victims or spectators in the incident. Depending on this, certain information will be entered such as the names of the victims or bullies involved. Attachments will then be uploaded to the database. 

Entity Relationship Diagram

Figure 9. Entity Relationship Diagram

The key in the users table is the main primary key in the database. The `id` attribute in the table is auto-incremented and creates a unique record for all users registered in the system. The `id` can also be seen as the common key that will be used by other associated tables.

  • users : The primary key `id` in the `users` table is auto-assigned to all registered users

  • students: In this table, the `user_id` acts as both the primary and the foreign key. Another `id` attribute is not required because there exists a direct mapping between each student profile and their user account. 

  • counselors: This table is similar to the students table with the `user_id` acting as both the primary key and the foreign key linking the counselor's profile to their corresponding user account.

  • admins: This table also uses the same principle where the `user_id` links the admin's profile to their respective user account.

  • vent_logs: In this table, the primary key is the `id` because more than one vent log can be submitted by one user. The `user_id` here acts as the foreign key.

  • bully_reports: Its primary key is `id`. There are three foreign keys present in it, which include `reporter_student_id`, `victim_student_id`, and `bully_student_id`. All three keys refer to `users.id`, and these keys are null because not all the names will be known.

  • audit_logs: The primary key of this table is `id`. There is a foreign key in this table as well, and that is `user_id`. 

  • sms_logs and email_logs: Both of these tables have `id` as their primary key. In these tables, `student_id` refers to `users.id`.

In conclusion, the tables of profile data of students, counselors, and admin have `user_id` as the primary and foreign key of `users` as well as one-to-one relationships. But in the case of logs and reports tables, they have their respective primary keys and foreign keys as well.

Use Case Diagram

Figure 10. Use Case Diagram

Figure 10 indicates how students, parents, counselors, and admins work with the reporting and notification functionalities of StudentShield.

Key Figures

  • Student: The main user who checks in to report incidents of bullying or create encrypted diary entries.

  • Counselor: School employees who check vent logs and look into bullying reports after logging in over a secure OTP gateway. When a student is flagged, they are the first to receive emergency emails and SMS alerts.

  • Super Admin: Uses the same OTP gateway to log in as well. They manage the system's audit logs, manage user accounts, and give a roles. They don't get direct alerts.

  • Parent: A passive actor who gets automated email and SMS alerts when the machine learning classifies their child's vent log as critical risk. 

Use Cases

  • Staff/Admin Login: This portal is used to authenticate counselors and administrators. Before providing access, an email-based OTP verification step is required.

  • Student Login: Students can log in separately and more easily with just their name and password. OTP is not necessary.

  • Submit Vent Log: Students write encrypted journal entries. The machine learning risk analyzer, which rates the text and determines a risk level (Low, Medium, High, or Critical), is automatically called for each submission.

  • Bully Report Submission: Students submit an encrypted incident report on bullying. The counselor office is instantly notified by email and SMS upon submission so they can look into it. 

  • View Counselor Dashboard / Review Vent Logs / Review Bully Reports: Counselor-side features for reading decrypted entries and managing active cases.

  • View Admin Dashboard / Manage Users & Roles / View System Audit Logs: Admin-side operate for account management and compliance tracking.

  • Trigger Email Alert / Trigger SMS Alert: Automated system replies that only extend from the submission use cases. The system emails and contacts the student's parent if a vent log receives a Critical score. The counselor office receives an instant email and SMS after filing a bully report. They work based on the backend and are not triggered through manual action by any of the actors. 

In the diagram provided below, you can see actions performed automatically by the system and those which have to be carried out manually by the user. The main reason for choosing this method is because all bully reports are instantly sent directly to the counselor's phone who must give approval first.

Requirements Analysis

1. Software Requirements

This is the software used for development, testing, and deployment of the StudentShield Web Application.

Development Tools and Frameworks:

  • Frontend Development 

    • HTML 5 

    • CSS 3 

    • Tailwind CSS (CDN)

    • Chart.js (risk distribution pie chart)

    • ApexCharts (vent trend area chart, student risk timeline)

    • JavaScript (Fetch API for AJAX)

  • Backend Development 

    • PHP 8.1+ (CodeIgniter 4 Framework) 

    • MySQL (via Laragon local server) 

    • Hugging Face Inference API (ML-based risk analysis) 

    • Local SMS Gateway (for automated SMS alerts to parents and counselors)

    • Gmail SMTP (for OTP delivery, parent email alerts, and counselor notifications)

  • Security and Authentication 

    • AES-256 Encryption (OpenSSL, for encrypting vent logs and incident reports at rest) 

    • Bcrypt Password Hashing (for storing user credentials) 

    • Email-based One-Time Password (OTP) verification for staff and admin logins 

    • Anti-spam rate limiting (30-second cooldown on vents, 120-second cooldown on bully reports) to prevent Local SMS Gateway credit abuse

    • Trusted Device Cookies (optional OTP bypass for remembered machines)

2. Hardware Requirements

This is the physical resource that will be required in developing, testing, and deploying the application.

Development Environment:

  • Developer Machines (for coding and testing): 

    • Processor: Minimum: Intel Core i3 / AMD Ryzen 3. 

    • RAM: 4 GB minimum; 8 GB recommended to handle Laragon, the browser, a code editor, and the local SMS gateway app running at the same time. 

    • Storage: Minimum: 128 GB SSD; Recommended: 256 GB SSD for the codebase, database files, and dependencies. 

    • Graphics: Integrated graphics (Intel HD or AMD Radeon Vega) are enough. No GPU-heavy tasks are required. 

    • Operating System: Windows 10 or later (Laragon is Windows-native).

3. SMS Gateway Device: 

Android Phone: Any Android 8.0+ device with an active SIM card and mobile data or Wi-Fi. This phone runs the local SMS gateway app that receives REST API calls from the server and sends actual text messages to parents.

Testing Devices:

  • Devices for Testing: 

    • Computer: Laptop or desktop with a modern browser for testing the full dashboard layout and responsiveness. 

    • Mobile Device: Any smartphone for testing the student-facing pages (vent form, bully report form) on small screens. 

    • Test Network: All devices must be on the same local network (Wi-Fi) so the web server can reach the Android SMS gateway.

Requirements Documentation

Functional Requirements

Role-Based Access Control

  • The system assigns three user roles: Student (role 0), Counselor (role 1), and Super Admin (role 2), each with different access levels.

  • Students can only access the student dashboard, the vent form, and the bully report form.

  • Counselors can view all vent logs, review bully reports, verify or reject incidents, and view student risk profiles.

  • Super Admins can do everything Counselors can, plus manage user accounts, assign roles, and view system audit logs.

  • User management is locked to Super Admin only (role 2). The code explicitly blocks Counselors from accessing it.

Account Management

  • Admin and Counselor accounts are pre-seeded or created by the Super Admin through the user management panel.

  • Student accounts are created by the Super Admin, who provides the student's name, student ID, section, adviser name, parent phone, parent email, and password.

  • Student IDs are mandatory for student accounts. Section and adviser name are also required.

  • Counselors and Super Admins log in with name and password, followed by a mandatory email-based OTP (6-digit code, 5-minute expiry).

  • Students log in with name and password only. No OTP is required.

  • Passwords are stored as bcrypt hashes. Legacy plaintext passwords are silently auto-upgraded on first login.

  • There is no password reset feature. If a user forgets their password, the Super Admin resets it manually through user management.

  • Super Admin generates profiles (Student and Parent information) which start out as "Pending Consent".

  • The first login requires accepting the Terms of Service (ToS) by opening a form.

  • Students must check off the box that he or she has submitted a signed Guardian Consent document before access can be granted.

Vent Log Submission and AI Risk Analysis

  • Students write personal journal entries through an encrypted submission form.

  • Each submission is sent to a custom ML model hosted on Hugging Face Spaces that scores the text and returns a risk level: Low, Medium, High, or Critical.

  • If the ML service is offline or times out (15 seconds), a local keyword-based fallback engine activates. This engine uses Filipino and English distress keywords with built-in Gen-Z sarcasm detection (e.g., "kms after math exam" is downgraded because it matches both a crisis keyword and an academic context marker).

  • All vent text is encrypted with AES-256 before being saved to the database.

  • If the risk level is Critical, the system automatically sends an SMS and email to the student's registered parent.

  • If the student checks "hide from parents" (domestic abuse precaution), parent alerts are suppressed and the counselor receives an emergency override notification instead.

  • A static and clearly visible privacy notice is placed immediately below the “Submit” button to ensure that students are aware of how their data will be handled.

  • This privacy notice informs students that their responses are securely stored by means of standard AES-256 encryption at rest, ensuring no data leaks occur.

  • Students are advised that their responses stay confidential unless they pose a “Critical” safety risk, in which case their parents or legal guardians will receive an instant SMS and email notification.

  • Should a case of domestic abuse be confirmed, the emergency alert will be directed not to the parents but directly to the school counselor.

Bully Report Submission (Two-Stage Alert Pipeline)

  • Students file encrypted bullying incident reports, identifying whether they are the victim or reporting for someone else.

  • The system resolves typed names to database user IDs using strict single-match lookups to prevent wrong-parent notification errors.

  • Stage 1 (Immediate): Upon submission, the counselor office gets an SMS and email alert so they can investigate. No parent alerts are sent yet.

  • Stage 2 (Counselor Verification): The counselor reviews the report on the dashboard and can click "Verify & Alert Parents," which fires automated SMS and email alerts to both the victim's parent and the bully's parent. Alternatively, the counselor can reject the report as fake, which blocks all parent alerts. They can also undo a decision to reset the report back to pending review.

Dashboard and Case Management

  • Counselors see all active vent logs with decrypted text, risk scores, student names, sections, and adviser information.

  • The dashboard displays a risk distribution pie chart (Chart.js) and a vent trend area chart (ApexCharts) that update in real time via AJAX polling.

  • Counselors can mark entries as Resolved, soft-delete (archive) them, restore archived entries, or perform bulk operations on multiple entries at once.

  • Counselors can click on any student name to open a full student profile that displays the student's information, their risk timeline graph (ApexCharts), all their vent history, and any bully report involvement.

  • The Admin dashboard provides user management (create, edit, delete), role assignment, and a full system audit log.

  • The Super Admin cannot demote or delete their own account (self-protection guard).

  • For making real-time interventions possible remotely, there is a direct video conference integration on the Counselor Dashboard. Once a critical-risk-scored student or a student with frequent risk occurrences is found, a counseling session can be arranged and a video conference link can be created and sent to the concerned student’s dashboard for conducting the session.

  • Counselors shall be able to generate a Case Summary Report for individual students. 

  • The report shall display the student's risk assessment history, highest recorded risk level, detected emotional indicators, bullying report statistics, notification history, counselor interventions, and current case status. 

  • The report shall serve as a centralized documentation record for counseling sessions, parent consultations, investigations, and intervention planning. 

  • The system shall allow counselors to view and export the report to pdf for record-keeping purposes. 

Automated Notifications

  • SMS alerts are sent through the Local SMS Gateway using app key and secret credentials stored in the .env configuration file.

  • Email alerts are sent through Gmail SMTP using credentials stored in the .env file.

  • A cooldown timer prevents alert fatigue by blocking duplicate notifications to the same parent within a set time window.

  • Alert logs are written to a JSON file and viewable from the dashboard.

Audit Logging

  • Every administrative action (resolve, archive, restore, bulk delete, verify, reject, undo, create user, update user, delete user) is logged to the audit_logs table with the acting user's ID, IP address, user agent string, and timestamp.

Data Retention Policy

  • Student records, vent logs, bullying reports, and notification logs shall remain active only while the student is officially enrolled in the institution.

  • In cases of graduation or official transfer to another school, all associated records shall be retained for thirty (30) days to allow completion of pending administrative and counseling processes.

  • After the 30-day retention period, the student's records shall be permanently deleted from the system database in accordance with the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (RA 10173).

  • Students who temporarily discontinue their studies, take a leave of absence, or become inactive shall not have their records deleted. Instead, their accounts shall be archived and marked as inactive.

  • Archived records shall remain encrypted and inaccessible to unauthorized users while stored within the system.

  • If the student re-enrolls in the institution, the archived account and records may be reactivated by authorized personnel to ensure continuity of counseling and case management services.

  • Access to retained and archived records shall be limited to authorized school personnel through role-based access controls.


Non-Functional Requirements

Performance

  • Vent submissions process and save within 2–3 seconds, including the round-trip to the Hugging Face ML API.

  • If the ML service times out (15-second limit), the local keyword fallback returns a risk score instantly.

  • Dashboard data refreshes via AJAX polling without requiring a full page reload.

Availability

  • High availability is ensured by deploying the core web application on InfinityFree Production Hosting. To maintain absolute reliability and sub-second response times if the Hugging Face Space is sleeping or offline, CodeIgniter 4 implements a native PHP fallback function (localKeywordFallback()) to evaluate student risk status locally without downtime.

  • Availability

Security

  • All sensitive text (vent content, incident details) is encrypted at rest using AES-256 via CodeIgniter's built-in encryption library.

  • User passwords are hashed with bcrypt. Plaintext passwords are never stored after first use.

  • Staff logins require a 6-digit OTP sent via email, with a strict 5-minute expiration.

  • Form submissions are rate-limited (30s for vents, 120s for bully reports) to prevent spam and gateway abuse.

  • The user management panel is access-controlled to Super Admin only. Counselors are explicitly blocked.

  • Under the requirements of the Data Privacy Act of 2012, the system must implement an automatic retention process for records. There should be no indefinite storage of any extremely sensitive information such as emotional trajectory data and unedited text logs, which should be automatically deleted or anonymized after the end of the school year.

Usability

  • The interface is built with Tailwind CSS and is responsive across desktop and mobile devices.

  • Students can submit a vent in 2 steps: type their entry and click submit.

  • The counselor dashboard loads all active cases in a single scrollable view with no pagination required.

Figure 11. Implementation Plan using Gantt Chart

The StudentShield system takes a three-layered cloud-based design that helps avoid machine learning latency issues while concentrating on reducing data security concerns and cost. It involves deployment of web application, machine learning service and emergency alert systems.

The proposed deployment will see students and counselors use a CodeIgniter 4 PHP-applications running on InfinityFree. This Hosting Company takes care of the Web server and the MySQL Database. Passwords will be hash-coded, audit records will be kept, plus vent submissions will be encrypted. It is set to be encrypted using AES-256 encryption from the set up prior to adding any raw text or bullying report. This will ensure that those without authorization to access the database will only be able to see random lengths of strings. This process will be done when updating a web application: push updates directly to web application via FTP, and clear system caches. The Hosting is free and for this reason, during the project phase is an opportunity for the project to be hosted at low cost provided that during the Test phase the code does not impose any restrictions on the type of Hosting used. If the school decides to expand the budget, or more users are needed for the system, the user can host the application and database for a fee at a different host (HostGator, AWS, DigitalOcean, etc.) and connect it to the custom domain name; the program need not be altered.

The machine power will play a significant role in the machine learning features allowing to run models (in the case of the machine learning features this will be Mdeberta, Go Emotions and the FAISS vector memory). As a result, the machine learning service employs a distinct entry and exit points as compared to the web app. The ML Engine is a containerized Python service built with FastAPI, running inside a Docker Container hosted on Hugging Face Spaces. The environment is stable and updates are easier thanks to running the service within a Docker container. Using Python scripts, the deployment is automated, whereby the older versions of the containers are removed to save disk space, other containers are zipped and transferred via SFTP, and the models are pushed into a Docker container via Hugging Face. However, on restarts, regardless of whether they are intentional or not, the API will continue to function. Last but not least, the system is interfaced with the device for the emergency notification purposes. For these regular email alerts which it transmits to parents and counselors via the Gmail SMTP protocol with an app password. If it is an emergency, the webapplication will send messages to the mobile phone, that will also be running an application for SMS-gateway within the local network. This phone will read the numbers out loud, and will text the parents/counsellors right away.

The implementation plan is a timeline of 10 months for the construction, deployment and testing of StudentShield. There are five phases of the project: Planning, System Coding, Debugging, System testing and user Acceptance Testing. During the three phases, each of the three key areas (Web app, ML service, automated alerts) are given a focus to ensure they operate in a coordinated system before the system goes live.

Statistical Treatment of Data

For assessing the efficiency, usability, and technology performance of StudentShield, an established process for gathering and analyzing data will be employed. The method for analysis is that of a mixed-method, wherein the researcher employs both qualitative and quantitative measures. Analysis of quantitative data gathered through evaluation of users will be accomplished through descriptive statistics. Additionally, in order to outline the methodology for measuring the effectiveness of the model during the next phase of implementation of the system, standard text classification measures are listed to assess the machine learning model's efficiency in future operation.

Data Gathering Technique

For an efficient evaluation of the StudentShield prototype, the following data collection techniques will be used by the researchers in assessing the design and usability of the prototype. The first approach that will be applied is the Questionnaire/Survey. This will require the utilization of ISO 25010 quality criteria when assessing the functionality, reliability, usability, and efficiency of the prototype. The second approach that will be applied is the Interview. The qualitative information will be gathered through this approach concerning the alerting functionalities of the prototype for the school staff members. The third approach that will be employed is the Observation. The usability of the mockup of the dashboard and the report form will be evaluated using this method by means of guided testing. Finally, the Document review approach will be adopted in order to determine whether the data fields and workflow of the prototype match those of the school guidance counseling manuals and paper forms.

Setting of the Study

The site or location wherein the research was conducted consists of the Saint Vincent Blessed School of Manila (SVBSM). This is the official Name of the organization that was partnered for the conduct of the experiment. Its Address / location is 732 Instruccion St., Sampaloc, Manila, 1000 Metro Manila. The Type of organization is a private learning institution that caters to the needs of junior high school students. The Number of employees/users in the organization includes those in the guidance counseling office and IT department that ensure the welfare of the junior high school students. The description of the environment where the system was applied or tested includes the selection of SVBSM as the main site of research because it was the client. The school administration collaborated with the researchers to come up with an incident reporting system that caters to their real-life problems.

Subject of the Study

The main subjects of the study in the prototype evaluation phase are categorized into three different user groups. These include all of the following groups involved in making the StudentShield work:

The Student Body: These would be the main users of the software that would use the "Vent" module and the incident reporting tool. The involvement of these users in the testing phase of the prototype would be essential to measure the usability, navigation, and security of the interaction with the system.

Guidance Counselors and Responders: These user categories will receive notifications for all incidents and will respond accordingly. Their participation in prototype evaluation is important for testing the administrative dashboard’s functionality and ease of navigation.

IT and System Administrators: These users are responsible for technical support operations on the platform. Their participation in prototype evaluation is important for assessing the system architecture, user experience flow, and compliance with data privacy requirements.

Sampling Technique

Non-probability sampling will be used in sampling respondents for prototype testing, namely purposive sampling. Purposive sampling is appropriate in the given case due to the fact that the project is in the prototype phase of development and the main goal of the research will be the receipt of quality feedback from potential users.


Purposive sampling will allow selecting those respondents who will correspond to the target characteristics of end-users. In particular, among the selected respondents, there should be guidance counselors that will work with the dashboard, technical security specialists, and some representatives from the student council who represent students.


Statistical Treatment of Data

The data acquired through the questionnaire is analyzed based on the statistical formula. In doing this, we can determine the average sentiment and the variance of opinions in the test population.

Frequency and Percentage

Frequency counts and percentages break down the demographic profile of the participants.

The formula for the percentage is as follows:

Formula: P = (f / n) × 100

Where:

  • P = percentage

  • f = frequency

  • n = total number of respondents

Weighted Mean

The weighted mean is computed to determine the measure of central tendency of each criterion. The weighted mean provides an estimate of how the system is rated by users. The formula for the weighted mean is as follows:

Formula: WM = (Σfx) / n

Where:

  • f = frequency

  • x = assigned weight of each scale point (1 to 5)

  • n = total number of respondents

The interpretation of the mean scores was based on the following scale:

Weighted Mean Range

Interpretation

4.21 - 5.00

Strongly Agree (Excellent)

3.41 - 4.20

Agree (Good)

2.61 - 3.40

Neutral (Fair)

1.81 - 2.60

Disagree (Poor)

1.00 - 1.80

Strongly Disagree (Very Poor)

Table 7: Mean Interpretation

Standard Deviation

Whereas the mean is an estimate of the average rating, the standard deviation measures agreement. Low standard deviation suggests that there was agreement among the participants, whereas high standard deviation suggests disagreement.

The formula for the standard deviation is as follows:

Formula: SD = √[ Σf(x - x̄)² / n ]

Where:

  • f = frequency of each rating

  • x = assigned weight of each scale point (1 to 5)

  • x̄ = mean of the distribution

  • n = total number of respondents

The interpretation of the standard deviation was based on the following scale:

Standard Deviation Range

Interpretation

2.00 and above

Very High Variability

1.50 - 1.99

High Variability

1.00 - 1.49

Moderate Variability

0.50 - 0.99

Low Variability

0.00 - 0.49

Very Low Variability

Table 8: Standard Deviation Interpretation

This statistical analysis gives an objective means of evaluating the user's acceptance of the system and overall system quality.

Confusion Matrix Metrics

Once the machine learning model undergoes full-scale testing with simulated datasets, the following standard classification metrics will be used to measure its diagnostic reliability:

  • Accuracy = (TP + TN) / Total

  • Precision = TP / (TP + FP)

  • Recall = TP / (TP + FN)

  • F1-Score = 2 × (Precision × Recall) / (Precision + Recall)

TP stands for true positive, TN stands for true negative, FP stands for false positive, and FN stands for false negative. These metrics will be used to examine the accuracy of the model in identifying potential threats in students' writing.
